title: 1988 AHSME Problem 21
statement: The complex number \(z\) satisfies \(z+\lvert z\rvert=2+8i.\) What is \(\lvert z\rvert^2?\) Note: if \(z=a+bi,\) then \(\lvert z\rvert=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}.\)

solutions.text:
Writing \(z=a+bi\) gives \(b=8\) and \(a+\sqrt{a^2+64}=2.\) Thus \(\sqrt{a^2+64}=2-a.\) Squaring yields \(a=-15.\) Therefore \(\lvert z\rvert^2=a^2+b^2=225+64=289.\)

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Use the real part to relate \(a\) to \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\)
